title: Working together with an rn-craft React Native app

R1.reason: A single baseQuery sets Authorization (Firebase ID token via getIdToken) and X-App-Locale from i18n.resolvedLanguage.

R2.reason: toApiError keeps code, status, requestId and Retry-After, and adds conflict and rateLimited kinds, noting the current ApiError lacks them.

R3.reason: applyFieldErrors maps details[].field to RHF setError, with dot paths, focus handling and a root.server fallback.

R4.reason: Uses infiniteQuery with the { data, meta } envelope, meta.nextCursor as the next page param, and transformResponse for single resources. It also covers filter keys and INVALID_CURSOR.

R5.reason: The backend users.id is used for Adapty identify and analytics, the Firebase uid stays server-side, and entitlements come from the backend via webhooks. Display premium from the Adapty SDK is a minor wrinkle.

R6.reason: Sign-out unlinks the device first and then resets the session. The backend re-binds tokens on account switch and scopes the DELETE by user.

R7.reason: One Idempotency-Key per user action, reused on retries. Auto-retry happens only when a key is present, and the key rotates only when the payload changes.

R8.reason: States up front that rn-craft's ApiError lacks code, requestId, conflict and rateLimited, and that everything is a proposed change. Lists what was not checked.

forbidden.item: Making rn-craft a dependency of the backend or the backend a dependency of the app
forbidden.evidence: The two sides are separate and connected only through the HTTP contract.

forbidden.item: Trusting isPremium or userId from the client
forbidden.evidence: States isPremium is never sent in a body, gating comes from GET /me backed by the server entitlements table, and the user comes from the verified token.

forbidden.item: Generating a new idempotency key on each retry
forbidden.evidence: The key is held in a ref and reused on every retry; it rotates only when the payload changes or after a definite failure.

forbidden.item: Claiming rn-craft already supports these headers or error cases
forbidden.evidence: Explicitly says the current ApiError has no code, requestId, conflict or rateLimited and that everything is a change.

grade.summary: Thorough, correct answer covering every rubric item with honest gap disclosure and no forbidden decisions.
